title: UI Layout Redesign — Community Research & Issue Collection (Web + Android)
purpose: Collect layout issues reported by the owner from the Android build, gather community best practices and skill guidance on what a finance-tracker layout should and should not include, and prepare inputs for the redesign discussion. No design decisions are made in this document — decisions happen in the discussion that follows.

inputs.user_report: 4 screenshots (Q1-Q4) from the installed Android APK, owner verdict: layout is not clean, collapsed, not user-friendly; full redesign needed for both Android app and web app

reported_issues.problem: Table rows are collapsed and cluttered. Company name wraps awkwardly, ISIN + purchase date + units crammed into one cell, a full-width gray attribute strip (Rating agency / Issuer type / Secured / Face value / Payout cycle / Broker) repeats under every row and eats vertical space. Not clean, not user-friendly.
reported_issues.owner_expectation: Clean, user-friendly layout and arrangement of holdings data.

reported_issues.problem: Received payments are shown as black tick marks (✓). Owner rejects ticks: every payment received should be marked GREEN; payment not received should be marked pending/danger in RED. This must follow the app's centralized color-coding theme (same pattern used everywhere).
reported_issues.owner_expectation: Centralized semantic color coding only: green = received, red/danger = unpaid/pending. No ad-hoc tick marks.

problems: Add Candidate form is a dense multi-row grid of 15+ fields — visually collapsed, no clear structure.
No autocomplete: typing an existing company name should show suggestions (system already locks duplicate ISIN and rejects incomplete company entries — the guard exists, UX does not).
ISIN and similar fields should auto-uppercase as the user types.
Credit rating should be a predefined select (full rating scale A..D / AAA..D) — not free text.
Candidate table bottom section is totally collapsed — buttons (Details / Move to Portfolio / Delete) wrap and stack badly, Action column overflows.
If a candidate has been invested (moved to Portfolio), it should no longer remain in the Watchlist.
reported_issues.owner_expectation: Clear form structure, friendly input assistance, rating dropdown, clean table with proper action layout, invested items auto-removed from watchlist.

problems: Header is crowded: theme switcher (System/Light/Dark), Hide amounts, Notifications badge (68) all compete for space.
Theme choice is duplicated — header toggle AND Settings > Appearance radio group say the same thing.
Owner wants a hide/unhide menu layout: user can collapse the menu to gain more viewing space, expand when needed.
Redesign must apply to BOTH the Android app and the web app (one shared UI).
reported_issues.owner_expectation: Space-saving collapsible/hideable menu, de-duplicated controls, clean header; unified redesign for web + Android.

community_research.summary: 11 sources: investment-dashboard UX guides (Medium/Lollypop/Aufait/KG Hub/Wolfpixel/Eleken), responsive-table references (James Ross/Setproduct/Ramotion/Appnroll/DEV), form-design (CXL/Adam Silver/Jotform), semantic-color systems (Eleken/GitHub design systems/Paleta/Carbon research), sidebar-navigation (Setproduct/DataCamp/arxiv dashboard patterns).
should_include: 3-5 KPI cards at top of dashboard (value + trend/color indicator), then charts, then detail tables — clear 3-zone hierarchy (top: attention numbers, middle: trends, bottom: detail)
Per-holding CARD as primary container on mobile: name, current value, gain/loss with color indicator — progressive disclosure for the rest (tap to expand)
Semantic status colors as TOKENS, one central helper: green = paid/received, amber = pending/due-soon, red = overdue/danger — applied identically in grid, payouts, badges, dashboard
Color + icon/text together (never color alone — accessibility + colorblind): green check icon + 'Paid' text, red dot + 'Unpaid'
Responsive table strategy: cards below ~768px, table on desktop; tap-row-to-expand for hidden columns (fits <= 8 columns)
Collapsible sidebar on desktop; below 768px: off-canvas drawer (~80-85% width) or bottom tab bar with 3-5 primary destinations + 'More' sheet
Form best practice: single-column on mobile, visible labels, autocomplete suggestions from existing companies (debounced), sensible defaults, inputmode=numeric for amounts
Predefined selects for bounded domains (credit rating scale, payout cycle, secured) — better than free text; auto-uppercase for ISIN
Tabular figures (fixed-width digits) for all money columns so numbers align
Hideable/collapsible navigation to reclaim content space (Vercel pattern: resizable hideable sidebar; every desktop destination gets a mobile home)
should_not_include: No dense multi-column tables shrunk onto phones (a 6-column table with horizontal scroll on mobile is a surrender, not a solution)
No gray full-width meta strips repeated under every row — use progressive disclosure (expand row/card)
No ad-hoc status glyphs (bare ticks, bare dots) outside the semantic color system
No duplicated controls (theme switcher in header AND in settings)
No widget/cram fest: every widget must map to a user decision — if it can't, it doesn't ship; avoid too many charts/tables competing for attention
No placeholder-as-label inputs; no free-text fields for values that have a fixed scale
No header clutter: every pixel of navigation is a pixel taken from data
No hover-only interactions on touch (Android): use tap-to-reveal
No color-only status (fails accessibility); no red used as decoration

design_system_suggestion.note: Skill auto-suggested Glassmorphism + Caveat/Quicksand handwriting fonts — REJECTED as unfit for a finance tracker (handwriting font harms trust and number legibility). Useful parts extracted below.
keep: Trust blue primary + profit green accent (fintech convergence: blue = navigation/trust, green = positive outcomes, red = real problems only)
Destructive red token #DC2626 reserved for genuine alerts
Anti-pattern: pure white backgrounds — use subtle surface tinting
Light + dark mode both required with 4.5:1 text contrast
design_system_suggestion.typography_direction: Professional sans-serif with tabular figures for money — NOT the skill's handwriting suggestion (to be confirmed in discussion)

ux_rules_applied: Tables on mobile: horizontal scroll OR card layout — never let wide tables break the viewport
Mobile-first: design 375px first, enhance at breakpoints
Autocomplete: show predictions as user types (debounced fetch + dropdown)
Every input needs a visible label; submit needs loading/success/error feedback
Status color must be paired with icon/text; contrast 4.5:1 body / 3:1 non-text
Bottom tabs max 5 items; extras go to More/Settings
Back behavior must be predictable (Android), modals need clear close

proposed_direction_for_discussion: 1. One centralized semantic status system (green/amber/red tokens + icon + label) used by grid, payouts, badges, dashboard — kills the tick-mark problem (Q2)
2. Holdings: desktop table with expandable rows; mobile = card stack with progressive disclosure — kills the gray meta strips (Q1)
3. Payouts matrix: keep table on desktop (frozen first column + horizontal scroll), mobile = per-bond cards with month chips colored by status; cells colored green/red/amber instead of ticks (Q1/Q2)

4. Watchlist: rebuild form single-column mobile / two-column desktop with autocomplete on Company, auto-uppercase ISIN, predefined rating select; candidate table → card layout on mobile; invested candidates auto-move out of watchlist (Q3)

5. Navigation: hideable sidebar (desktop) + drawer or bottom-tabs (mobile) with 3-5 primary destinations; single theme control (move to user menu, remove duplication); notifications + hide-amounts move into a compact overflow menu (Q4)
6. Same templates serve web and Android (WebView) — one redesign, both surfaces; verify at 375px / 768px / 1440px
next_step: DISCUSS with owner: review Q1-Q4 + community include/exclude lists, confirm direction items 1-6, then author design artifacts (wireframes) and issues.
